## Upgrading from v0.7.0

**`oinkie reaggregate` is now `oinkie review`.** Aggregation is no longer all
that the command is for, so the name stopped fitting. The options are the same;
only the default of `-d/--dest-file` changes, from `reaggregate.csv` to
`review.csv`.

```sh
# before
oinkie reaggregate -A topn:3 -d out/top3.csv out/
# after
oinkie review -A topn:3 -d out/top3.csv out/
```

The old name is not an alias. It is a hidden subcommand that refuses, says
`review` and exits non-zero, and it will be removed in the next minor release.

**The MCP tool `oinkie_reaggregate` is now `oinkie_review`**, with no old name
kept, so `tools/list` holds one tool rather than two of which a model could not
tell which is deprecated.

The documentation page moved to `usage/review/`; the old address redirects.

**The library no longer knows the command line.** Code that uses `oinkie` as a
library is affected; the `oinkie` command is not, and its `--help`, `info` and
shell completions are byte-for-byte what they were.

- `Ir`, `Algorithm` and `PairingStrategy` no longer derive clap's `ValueEnum`.
  Each has an `ALL` constant listing its variants, and `Algorithm` implements
  `FromStr`, which reads either spelling of a name (`weightedjaccard` or
  `weighted-jaccard`) in any case.
- `Error::Clap` is gone. A usage error is the command line's own type now.
- `Error::ToolNotFound { tool, env, candidates }` is new: a lifting tool whose
  installation could not be found. It replaces a `Parse` whose text told the
  reader to pass `--home`, which only the command line has; `oinkie lift` still
  says exactly what it said.
- `Algorithm::cli_name` is now `Algorithm::name`: it is the algorithm's name
  inside an analysis name, which is not a command-line matter.
- `BirthmarkType::advertised`, `BirthmarkType::description`,
  `AnalysisType::advertised_names` and `MAX_ADVERTISED_K` are gone: they existed
  to feed completion and `--help`. `BirthmarkType::all(max_k)` lists every
  family with k-grams up to a ceiling the caller chooses.
- `extractor::dest_file_name` is gone. The file name an extraction is written
  to is the command line's to decide.
- `Lifter` has a `notice` method, which returns something the user is owed
  before the first lift. The IDA lifter returns its cloud-upload disclosure
  there instead of printing it; the `oinkie` command still prints it to stderr
  before the first lift, where `--level` cannot hide it.
- **`oinkie::prelude` is gone, and every name has one path.** The root holds
  `Program`, `Error` and `Result`; everything else is in the module it belongs
  to:

  ```rust
  use oinkie::Program;
  use oinkie::birthmarks::{Birthmark, BirthmarkType, AnalysisType};
  use oinkie::compare::{Aggregator, Algorithm, Comparator, PairingStrategy};
  use oinkie::extract::Extractor;
  use oinkie::lift::{Ir, LifterBuilder};
  ```

  `oinkie::extractor` is now `oinkie::extract`. `compare::Size`, the payload of
  `Aggregator::TopN`, can be named for the first time.
- **`AnyProgram` is now `Program`, and the generic `Program<T>` is no longer
  public.** A program is read with `Program::load`, which picks the operation
  type from the file, and is opaque: a new lifter is no longer a breaking change
  to it. `Extractor::extract_any` is now `Extractor::extract`, and
  `Comparator::compare_any` is now `Comparator::compare_programs`. The generic
  `Extractor::extract`/`extract_each` and `Comparator::compare_programs` taking a
  `Program<T>` are gone with it, as are `Function<T>`, the `Op` and `Iterable`
  traits, and the `ghidra`, `ida` and `binaryninja` modules, which held only
  the per-representation operation types.
- **`Elements` is now `birthmarks::Function`**, and the types say what the
  terms say (#131): a `Birthmark` holds one `Function` per function, and a
  `Function` -- one function's birthmark -- is made of elements, its `Data`.
  `Birthmark::functions()` returns them, replacing iteration through the
  `Iterable` trait; `Function::len()` counts a function's elements and
  `Birthmark::len()` the functions. There is no `Elements` alias: the old name
  was only reachable through the prelude, which is gone. **Birthmark files keep
  the key `elements`**, so every file written before still loads, and files
  written now load in v0.7.0.
- **The fields of `Birthmark`, `Function` and `AnalysisType` are private**, so
  a later change to how a birthmark is held is not a breaking one. Use the
  accessors: `name`, `path`, `ir`, `birthmark_type`, `extracted_at`,
  `duration`, `json_path` and `functions` on `Birthmark`; `name` and `data` on
  `Function`; `birthmark` and `comparator` on `AnalysisType`. `Metadata` is no
  longer public; everything in it is reachable through those accessors.
- No longer public, because nothing outside the crate had a use for them:
  `lift::HomeSpec`, `Ir::home_spec`, `Ir::find_home` (`LifterBuilder` is the way
  in), `BirthmarkType::with_shape`, `Birthmark::check_comparable_with` (the
  comparator calls it), `Metadata::parse`, `Comparison::new` and
  `Error::error_or`. `Birthmark::comparable_with` is removed.
- **`Error`, `Ir`, `BirthmarkType`, `Algorithm`, `Aggregator` and
  `PairingStrategy` are `#[non_exhaustive]`.** A `match` on any of them outside
  this crate needs a wildcard arm. In exchange, a new error, representation,
  birthmark family, algorithm, aggregator or strategy is no longer a breaking
  change. To enumerate what exists, use `Ir::ALL`, `Algorithm::ALL`,
  `PairingStrategy::ALL` or `BirthmarkType::all`. `Data` stays exhaustive on
  purpose: a new birthmark shape changes what every consumer has to do with it,
  so it should stop the build.
- **`Error::is_caller_fault()`** says whether the caller could have avoided an
  error by asking differently -- a name, a pairing or a number they gave, or a
  file they named. It is the classification the MCP server answers with, moved
  into the library because only the crate that defines `Error` can still match
  it exhaustively.
- **`Error::ToolIo(path, cause)` is new**, and `Error::Io` now means an I/O
  failure on a path the caller gave. Starting a lifting tool and writing its
  scratch files used to report `Io`; they report `ToolIo`, which reads the
  same but is not counted as the caller's fault.
- **The score CSV is the command line's.** `Comparison::store`, the `CsvInfo`
  trait, `Metadata::csv_info` and `escape_csv_string` are gone from the
  library; `oinkie compare`, `run` and the MCP server write the same files as
  before. A library user who wants a comparison written down has what it is
  made of instead: `Comparison::columns`, `rows` and `matrix`, alongside
  `similarity` and `duration`, and the new accessors `Birthmark::ir`,
  `Birthmark::json_path`, `Program::json_path`, `Program::symbol_count` and
  `Program::function_names`.
- **A carriage return in a path or a function name is quoted in the score
  CSV.** It ends a record as surely as a line feed, and was left bare, so a
  name containing one split its line and `review` read back a truncated path.
- `clap` and `sha2` are optional dependencies behind the `cli` feature, which
  `gencomp` and `mcp` now imply. `cargo add oinkie --no-default-features` pulls
  in neither.

## Highlights

- **`reaggregate` is renamed `review`** (#132).
- **The library does not depend on the command line** (#133).
